column1: ## ODI nanopore cohort -- ENA PRJEB42910 / ERP126837 (Street et al. 2022, JCM)
## This is the DEPLETION cohort, selected on sequencing yield. For the AMR
## cohort -- S. aureus specimens selected from the paper's own ground truth --
## see amr_cohort.tsv. Yield turned out to be a poor proxy for S. aureus
## content: only patients 119 and 103 below are S. aureus.
## Pulled from the ENA run report, confirmed via BV-BRC SRA metadata.
## All rows are Oxford Nanopore GridION, WGS, SINGLE layout, taxon 256318.
## prep: sap = 5% saponin differential lysis
##       fil = 5-micrometre filtration
## Three of the six high-yield saponin runs have a filtration partner from the
## SAME patient specimen. The raw yield gap is dramatic before any mapping:
##   patient_22    4.16 Gb sap  vs  0.034 Gb fil   -- 121x
##   patient_103   3.82 Gb sap  vs  0.016 Gb fil   -- 240x
##   patient_72    5.37 Gb sap  vs  0.144 Gb fil   --  37x
## Yield alone is not the paper's claim, though -- the claim is about the
## HUMAN FRACTION. Two aliquots can differ in total yield for ordinary
## library reasons. The test that matters is the microbial yield and pathogen
## breadth after mapping, which is what 05_depletion_summary.py computes.
## CAVEAT: these are the deposited NON-HUMAN reads. Street et al. state only
## reads "classified as nonhuman" were submitted. So the absolute human
## fraction is NOT recoverable from this deposit -- host depletion already
## happened, then host reads were stripped again before upload. Do not report
## a "% human" figure from these files and call it a reproduction of Table 1.
## Columns: run_accession  patient  prep  reads  bases  role
